report.title: Checkout slowdown: inventory DB pool acquisition waits
report.summary: Checkout p95 latency and API errors increased during the window. Slow traces show checkout time dominated by inventory reserve waiting on a DB connection pool. A recent release reduced the inventory client pool max, which is temporally consistent with increased pool contention.

findings.text: checkout-api p95 rose to 2840ms with API errors up to 6.8%, while request rate stayed near 120 rps.
Representative slow trace shows inventory.reserve dominating checkout time, with 2190ms spent in db.pool.acquire; 18/20 slow samples show pool waits >1800ms.

Dependency metrics show payment authorization latency and database CPU near baseline, while pool pending requests rose to 84, consistent with connection pool contention rather than provider/CPU saturation.
A 14:12 release changed the inventory client connection pool maximum from 20 to 5; latency increase begins around 14:15, supporting (but not proving) the pool-limit-change hypothesis.

nextSteps: Confirm current inventory client and inventory-db pool configuration, including max connections, timeouts, and queue depths, and compare to the pre-14:12 baseline settings.
Validate whether pool contention aligns with traffic patterns by correlating pool-pending, db.pool.acquire duration, and checkout latency across the 14:00–14:30 window.
Ask Inventory Services to review release 8f2c1d for the pool-max reduction and prepare an owner-approved revert if it matches the current config and no other constraints block it.
report.uncertainty: Slow-trace sampling indicates many slow requests wait on pool acquisition, but it does not prove all requests are affected. The release timing is correlational; other concurrent factors could contribute without additional config and saturation measurements.
report.customerUpdate: We’re seeing elevated checkout latency and some API errors. Current traces indicate the delay is primarily while reserving inventory, specifically waiting to acquire a database connection. We’re verifying whether a recent configuration change reduced connection pool capacity; this is not yet confirmed as the sole cause.

report.title: INC-0242: Payment-path latency and errors after deploy
report.summary: Evidence does not support the latest deploy as the primary driver of payment errors. Errors and elevated latency appear across old and new checkout cohorts, while slow traces concentrate time in the payment authorization call, including one representative upstream 504.

findings.text: Checkout p95 latency and error rate increased in the window, while request rate stayed stable.
Old and new checkout release cohorts show similar elevated latency and error rates, which is inconsistent with a deploy-only regression.
In a representative slow trace, most time is in payments.authorize (2880ms of 3210ms) and it includes one upstream HTTP 504.
17 of 20 slow sampled traces show slow payment authorization, consistent with a dependency-side or network-path issue affecting the payment step.

nextSteps: Review cohort-split metrics and error breakdown for checkout-api around 15:18 UTC to confirm impact is uniform across versions and endpoints.
Investigate payment-provider connectivity from checkout-api (timeouts, DNS/TLS handshakes, egress errors) and correlate with the sampled slow authorization spans.
Have the Payments team request provider-side status and logs; if they propose a reversible mitigation (e.g., traffic shaping or timeout tuning), it requires their approval before any change.
report.uncertainty: Provider-side telemetry and a confirmed provider incident report are unavailable, so the payment-provider’s behavior cannot be confirmed from our data alone. The single observed 504 is one trace example, and sampled traces represent only a subset of slow requests.
report.customerUpdate: Between 15:00–15:30 UTC we saw elevated checkout latency and payment failures. Our traces show most delay during the payment authorization step; we do not yet have confirmation from the external payment provider, and we are continuing to validate where the slowdown originates.

report.title: INC-0244: next dependency check for checkout slowness
report.summary: Checkout latency and errors rose around 17:14 UTC, with traces concentrating delay in inventory’s database connection handshake. Network telemetry shows increased rejected connections on the inventory-to-db path after a firewall policy update. Next investigation should focus on that network-policy path owned by Network Platform.

findings.text: Checkout p95 increased to 3180ms and error rate to 7.4% while request rate stayed ~115 rps; both old and new checkout release cohorts degraded similarly.
In 16/20 slow sampled traces, inventory spends >2000ms in the database connection handshake (representative trace shows tcp.connect 2450ms) while query and pool-acquire times are near baseline.
Path-scoped flow records show 18% rejected connections from inventory subnet to inventory-db:5432 vs 0.1% baseline, and a firewall policy update occurred on that path shortly before degradation.

Database and payment latencies for successful operations are near baseline; these measurements don’t cover failed connection attempts and don’t localize the fault beyond the connection-establishment phase.

nextSteps: Network Platform should review the 17:11 firewall policy update on the inventory-to-database path and validate which rules are rejecting inventory→inventory-db:5432 connections during the incident window.

Data Platform and Inventory Services should correlate database server logs (connection attempts/refusals/timeouts) with the network flow rejects to confirm whether failures occur before reaching Postgres.
Checkout Experience should compare checkout error modes against inventory timeouts to quantify how much checkout degradation tracks the inventory DB connection establishment delay.
report.uncertainty: Flow rejects and slow traces are consistent with a network-policy issue, but there is no request-level linkage between individual rejected flows and the traced requests, and no device-level counters or packet captures to localize where rejects occur.
report.customerUpdate: We’re seeing elevated checkout latency and errors during the window. The delay in our traces is concentrated in connecting from inventory to its database, and network telemetry shows increased connection rejects on that path, but we have not confirmed the exact mechanism yet.
